adversarial_assessment: The claim that local animals need not be independently viable is supported by paragraph55. It should not itself be identified as an error.

The subsequent categorical dismissal of German conservation status, on the ground that the European metapopulation is favourable, is materially different. Paragraphs47–48 and the operative answer in66 expressly retain local and national assessment and prohibit masking unfavourable national status by an exclusively cross-border assessment.

The strongest rescue is that the author means an unfavourable German status assessed in isolation cannot be decisive. That is consistent with55 in principle. However, the unqualified following dismissal and objection to the draft giving German status any decisive role go beyond that limited point.
Cross-border exchanges can change the national assessment itself. The correction must not require biological national self-sufficiency or assume that German status actually is unfavourable.

This is an account of a specified judgment and the source-to-claim mismatch, not a new legal opinion about whether any particular hunt is lawful. The draft already permits specified intervention even under unfavourable status; do not describe every form of wolf hunting as categorically barred.
severity_and_direction: Major/true is defensible because the source description is a central premise for removing the conservation-status objection to regular hunting. This does not independently establish current German wolf status, the appropriate hunting regime or policy outcomes.
